A zero index would let us retain how neighboring gaps and exterior interactions evolve together. That may address the correlation lost when we replace the whole evolution by one \(K\) floor. Yes. The useful formulation is **\(M_n(p,q,t)\), with \(n\) indexing the adjacent pair \((x_n,x_{n+1})\)**. All rows must describe the same underlying zeros.

Writing \(g_n=x_{n+1}-x_n\), the existing hierarchy gives
\[
g_n'=\frac4{g_n}-2g_nM_n(1,1).
\]
Neighboring rows also satisfy exact compatibility relations, for example
\[
M_n(2,0)+\frac1{g_n^2}
=
M_{n+1}(0,2)+\frac1{g_{n+1}^2}.
\]
Both sides describe the same moment anchored at their shared zero. These constraints are what make the additional index mathematically useful.

There is also a block cancellation: summing gap-weighted interactions leaves only two boundary forces. That retains correlations lost by independent moment bounds. The remaining difficulty is converting such aggregate control into protection of **each individual gap**.
